page: Microsoft Azure EC8ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions), VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance includes 322 GB of local SSD temporary storage, providing direct low-latency disk capacity alongside standard Azure remote storage capabilities. Network provisioning does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing or allocated IPs for internet-facing connectivity. There are no discrete hardware acceleration GPUs attached.

In synthetic computing benchmarks, the AMD EPYC 9V74 silicon exhibits strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25 percent for both stress-ng single-core tests (3022.86) and Geekbench 6 single-core routines (1937.0). Multi-core throughput aligns with expectations for an 8-vCPU footprint, achieving middle-tier results across stress-ng multi-core (12056.83) and Geekbench multi-core (7291.0). In application tests, Geekbench text processing performed in the upper quartile (2526.0), while Clang software compilation (9660.0), image processing (6335.0), and PassMark database operations (3718.39) landed in the middle 50 percent.

From an efficiency standpoint, the EC8ads_v6 offers strong compute density per core combined with an elevated RAM ceiling and bundled high-speed scratch storage. Workloads benefit from the high single-thread responsiveness without needing to over-provision vCPUs solely to gain additional memory. This profile fits relational databases, medium-scale in-memory key-value caches such as Redis, enterprise Java applications, and memory-constrained analytical data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure EC8ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores, 64.0 GB of system memory, and a 322 GB local SSD scratch volume. It includes support for modern vector instructions like AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, though it contains no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core capabilities, achieving top-quartile performance in stress-ng and Geekbench single-thread routines, while overall multi-core computation, compilation, and memory benchmarks perform within the median range. In-memory throughput remains solid, evidenced by Redis achieving 10.34 million operations per second. The balanced 8 GB RAM per vCPU allocation and fast local disk make the EC8ads_v6 well matched for transactional databases, Redis caching layers, analytical data processing, and enterprise application servers requiring solid per-thread performance alongside ample memory capacity.
